title: Yara and the Debt
premise: Ulyana Sterling built her career tracing dirty money for the Financial Conduct Authority, but after the incident — a raid that left a witness dead and Ulyana's name quietly scrubbed from the record — she was moved into a safe house and given only clean, meaningless casework to keep her docile. When she finds the safe house listed online with interior photos that include her own handwriting on a whiteboard, she realizes her handlers are burning her cover, either to flush out the network that trained her or to erase her as a loose end. Over seventy-two hours leading to the Frankfurt market open, Ulyana turns investigator on her own life, following laundered money backward through shell companies to the man who made her: her mentor, Aldous Vane. She must choose between exposing him and protecting Tomas, the analyst she loves who unknowingly sits inside Vane's web. In the end, Ulyana burns the network by feeding its own ledger to regulators worldwide, lets Vane walk into a trap of his own design, and accepts that survival cost her the clean hands she once believed in.
about_author: Kestrel Villalobos is a former compliance officer who spent nine years untangling cross-border money flows before trading spreadsheets for sentences. They write thrillers about people who discover the systems they serve were never on their side.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Scrolling property sites at 3 a.m., she finds her safe house for sale — twelve photos, including her whiteboard scrawl of account numbers. The emotional beat is cold recognition: someone wanted her to see this. She photographs everything and begins a private file she cannot officially open.

chapters.title: Clean Hands, Dirty Nights
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, flashback-laced. At the office she processes a trivial case while colleagues avoid her eyes; the incident is an unspoken wall. Her handler, Merrick, reassures her the listing is 'a vendor error.' The beat is suffocating normalcy — she performs calm while cataloguing every lie.

chapters.title: Tomas
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. A junior analyst at a Frankfurt clearing firm notices a recurring settlement pattern that shouldn't exist and emails his old mentor — Ulyana. His beat is earnest curiosity, the reader seeing the trap being baited before he does. He books a flight to London without telling his supervisor.

chapters.title: The Vendor Error
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She traces the estate agency behind the listing to a shell company whose registered director died in 2019 — yet signed documents last month. Someone is using dead identities she recognizes from training files. Beat: dread sharpening into purpose; the hunt has reversed direction.

chapters.title: What Merrick Knows
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Merrick meets an unnamed superior and requests 'the Sterling option,' believing he's protecting her. Ulyana, meanwhile, tails Merrick to a private members' club and photographs him meeting Aldous Vane — the man who recruited her, presumed retired. Beat: betrayal reframes everything.

chapters.title: The Training House
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, past and present braided. She returns to the unmarked building in Rotherhithe where Vane taught recruits to think like launderers. It's now a co-working space, but the basement door lock is unchanged. Inside she finds her own training dossier, annotated in fresh ink. Beat: grief and fury entwined.

chapters.title: Arrival
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. He lands in London and calls Ulyana against protocol; she meets him in a rain-soaked car park and tells him almost nothing, but takes his data. Their charged history surfaces. Beat: love rekindling under operational paranoia — she needs him and hates needing him.

chapters.title: Seventy-Two Hours
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Decoding Tomas's settlement pattern, she maps a laundering pipeline timed to settle at Friday's Frankfurt open — a two-billion-euro wash disguised as a currency hedge. Whoever controls it controls the narrative of her 'incident.' Beat: the clock starts; stakes become concrete.

chapters.title: The Incident, Retold
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, full flashback. The raid, the dead witness, and the truth she buried: the operation was fed deliberately bad intel — by Vane — to create a scapegoat. She was never collateral damage; she was the product. Beat: devastating self-reckoning that converts guilt into resolve.

chapters.title: Merrick's Warning
chapters.summary: Merrick's POV. Torn between loyalty and conscience, he warns Ulyana to stop digging, revealing that 'the Sterling option' means permanent relocation — or worse. She realizes he genuinely believes he's saving her. Beat: tragic midpoint; even her enemies think they're kind.

chapters.title: Dead Director, Live Signature
chapters.summary: Ulyana and Tomas's alternating POV. Working from a hotel room, they match the forged signatures to a handwriting style Vane drilled into trainees — including Ulyana's own. The frame-up is designed to look like her work. Beat: intimate horror; the trap wears her face.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Following the pipeline's origin node, Tomas accesses a legacy server and finds the master ledger — every payment Vane's network ever cleaned, including bribes to the officials who closed Ulyana's case. He copies it to a drive. Beat: triumph curdling as alarms trip behind him.

chapters.title: Run
chapters.summary: Alternating POV chase chapter. Tomas flees across London with the drive; Ulyana runs interference through the City's back streets. They reunite but know both are now marked. Beat: adrenaline and tenderness — in crisis, duty and love finally point the same direction.

chapters.title: Vane
chapters.summary: Vane's POV, first time. Charming, patient, utterly amoral, he reviews Ulyana's progress with something like pride and orders the Frankfurt leg accelerated. He offers Merrick a way out that requires abandoning her. Beat: chilling intimacy with the antagonist; we see how easily he once seduced Ulyana's ambition.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Vane summons her to a gallery after hours and offers reinstatement, absolution, and protection — if she returns the ledger and testifies that Tomas acted alone. He speaks of survival as the only honest currency. Beat: temptation rendered sincerely; the price of survival made explicit.

chapters.title: What Love Costs
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Learning the full shape of Ulyana's past, he urges her to take the deal and vanish; she refuses. Their argument becomes a confession — each would rather burn than be saved by the other's ruin. Beat: love against duty, stated plainly and painfully.

chapters.title: Counterfeit Morning
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She pretends to accept Vane's terms, handing over a doctored drive while distributing fragments of the real ledger to regulators in five jurisdictions, timed to release at the Frankfurt open. Beat: cold competence; the investigator becomes the instrument.

chapters.title: Frankfurt Open
chapters.summary: Multi-POV crescendo. Markets open; the wash transaction triggers; the ledger fragments land simultaneously. Vane's network seizes up mid-transfer as freezes cascade across accounts. Merrick, choosing at last, feeds Ulyana the final access code. Beat: controlled detonation of the entire plot.

chapters.title: The Man Who Made Me
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Confronting Vane in the gallery as his empire collapses around his phone, she refuses his final offer — a partnership. He notes, almost fondly, that she was his best work. She leaves him for the arriving officers rather than the violence he expects. Beat: climax resolved by refusal, not gunfire.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Merrick's POV. Internal affairs descends; Merrick gives a full statement, accepting his own ruin as penance. Ulyana watches him led away and understands mercy and justice rarely share a room. Beat: somber accounting; every choice priced and paid.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She testifies publicly, surrendering her anonymity and her clean record together, naming her own complicity alongside Vane's crimes. Tomas waits outside. Beat: catharsis through exposure — survival finally means telling the truth, not hiding from it.

chapters.title: Yara and the Debt
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, epilogue. Months later, sleeping through the night for the first time since the incident, she reads that the safe house sold to a young family. On her desk: a new case file, real dirt in it. She opens it. Beat: quiet renewal — the debt paid, the work honestly begun.
